title: Dimensional’s Approach to Asset Allocation | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional lays out its house allocation framework: start from the global market cap portfolio, tilt systematically toward size, value, and profitability rather than timing them, size fixed income to the investor's volatility tolerance, and deviate from market weights only for implementation and tax reasons (US home bias, currency hedging on bond-heavy books, REITs out of taxable accounts, municipal bonds in). The explicit stance is that no short-term shifts across premiums, regions, countries, or sectors are made, and that optimizer-driven capital market assumptions are inferior to a science-based framework.

insights.claim: Adding fixed income to an equity portfolio is presented as the single most effective lever available for balancing a total portfolio's expected volatility against its expected return, ahead of any security-selection or timing decision.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Treat the bond weight, not manager selection, as the primary risk dial when a client's volatility tolerance changes.
insights.quote: adding fixed income to an equity portfolio is one of the most effective tools an investor can use to balance the expected volatility and returns of the total portfolio
insights.locator: Asset Allocation Between Equity and Fixed Income

insights.claim: Three allocation archetypes are mapped to three distinct goals: all-equity or equity-heavy for asset growth, a 60% equity / 40% fixed income mix for total return from capital appreciation plus current income, and predominantly fixed income for capital preservation.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The 60/40 is framed here as a goal-specific solution, not a default — a useful check when defending or replacing it in a model lineup.
insights.locator: For investors focused on the growth of assets

insights.claim: In high-equity portfolios, extending bond duration and accepting lower credit quality adds expected return without materially raising total portfolio volatility, because equities already dominate the volatility budget.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Argues for barbell-style term and credit risk in the bond sleeve of aggressive portfolios — the opposite of the instinct to keep bonds safe everywhere.
insights.locator: Emphasis on Known Drivers of Higher Expected Returns

insights.claim: In fixed-income-heavy portfolios the stated objective is preserving consumption power, which argues for short duration, high credit quality, and explicit inflation protection rather than reaching for yield.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Conservative mandates should hold TIPS-like exposure and short duration; credit and term risk belong in the aggressive sleeves instead.
insights.locator: In portfolios with higher fixed income allocations

themes.theme: Global Market Portfolio as the Anchor

insights.claim: The theoretical global market portfolio — all securities held at market capitalization weights — is proposed as the default regional starting point because it embeds the aggregate expectations of all market participants and updates continuously.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Any regional overweight becomes an active bet requiring an explicit justification, which shifts the burden of proof onto home-country tilts.
insights.locator: Asset Allocation Across Regions

insights.claim: There is no reliable evidence that the relative performance of one country or region versus another can be predicted in advance, even though regions can diverge sharply over short horizons.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Undercuts the tactical regional rotation trade; short-horizon US-vs-international divergence is framed as noise, not signal.
insights.quote: there is no reliable evidence that the performance of one country or region relative to another can be predicted in advance
insights.locator: While both regions offer the potential

insights.claim: The only reasons offered for overweighting the US beyond market cap weight are implementation and tax frictions — not any forecast of superior US returns.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Reframes home bias as a cost-optimization decision, so it should be sized to actual tax and withholding drag rather than to conviction about US outperformance.
insights.locator: There may, however, be sensible reasons to deviate

insights.claim: Foreign dividend tax withholding creates a performance drag on international holdings inside non-taxable or tax-deferred accounts, a cost that cannot be reclaimed the way it can in some taxable structures.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Account location matters: pushing international equity into IRAs and 401(k)s silently forfeits withholding credits.
insights.locator: For example, foreign dividend tax withholding

insights.claim: High-bracket investors can lower tax costs by overweighting US equities inside taxable accounts, driven by lower US dividend yields and some managers' ability to suppress realized capital gains within equity funds.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The after-tax case for US overweighting scales with the investor's bracket — a mechanical, measurable input rather than a market view.
insights.locator: Investors in higher tax brackets may also be able

insights.claim: Currency hedging meaningfully reduces portfolio volatility for fixed-income-heavy allocations but does not meaningfully reduce return volatility for equity-heavy allocations, per cited 2020 research by Wei Dai and Warwick Schneller.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Hedging costs are worth paying on international bonds and largely wasted on international equity — a concrete screen when choosing hedged vs. unhedged share classes.
insights.quote: for equity-heavy allocations, hedging currencies does not meaningfully reduce return volatility
insights.locator: Another important consideration when investing globally

insights.claim: The hedging decision is framed as contingent on the asset allocation itself rather than on any view of currency direction, with short-term protection against large swings acknowledged only as a preference some investors hold.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Implies no tactical FX overlay; hedge ratios should be set by the bond/equity mix and left alone.
insights.locator: Investors should base currency hedging decisions

insights.claim: Valuation theory links a firm's expected future cash flows to its current price through a discount rate, generating the prediction that small cap beats large cap, low relative price beats high relative price, and high profitability beats low profitability.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The three-premium framework is derived from a pricing identity rather than backtests, which is the argument for its persistence out of sample.
insights.locator: Equities Valuation theory provides a framework

insights.claim: The size, value, and profitability premiums are documented in studies spanning more than 40 countries and nine decades of stock data, citing Fama and French plus Novy-Marx's gross profitability work.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The breadth claim (40+ countries, 90 years) is the specific evidentiary bar to hold competing factor products against.
insights.locator: Consistent with valuation theory, the existence of these premiums

insights.claim: Profitability is defined precisely as operating income before depreciation and amortization, minus interest expense, scaled by book equity — not as ROE, margins, or free cash flow.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Two 'quality' funds using different profitability definitions will hold materially different names; check the metric before assuming overlap.
insights.quote: Profitability is measured as operating income before depreciation and amortization minus interest expense scaled by book equity.
insights.locator: Footnote 5

insights.claim: No short-term allocation shifts are made across premiums, regions, countries, or sectors, because research has not found that short-term performance differences among them can be consistently predicted.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: A manager publicly precommitting against rotation means tracking error versus the market will come from persistent tilts, not from timing calls.
insights.quote: we do not make short-term allocation shifts across premiums, regions, countries, or sectors
insights.locator: Based on these findings

insights.claim: Attempting to time differences across premiums or regions raises turnover and trading costs and can increase return volatility, mechanically raising the performance hurdle a timing strategy must clear to be worthwhile.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Evaluate any tactical overlay against a cost-inflated hurdle, not against a zero-friction benchmark.
insights.quote: A strategy that attempts to time these differences may increase return volatility and incur higher turnover and trading costs relative to a consistent approach
insights.locator: A strategy that attempts to time these differences

insights.claim: Realized returns differ across premiums, regions, countries, and sectors, but those differences are not reliable over the long term, which is the stated justification for integrating all three premiums simultaneously rather than picking one.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Argues against single-factor products and against concentrating a factor tilt in one region.
insights.locator: Realized returns vary across the premiums

insights.claim: Using current market prices to identify expected-return differences is positioned as a middle path that escapes both the rigidities of index tracking and the unreliability of forecasting.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The pitch is explicitly against pure indexing as well as against forecasting-based active — relevant when a lineup is being framed as index vs. active.
insights.quote: we can avoid the rigidities of indexing as well as the unreliability of forecasting
insights.locator: Asset Allocation Across Securities

insights.claim: Expected returns in bonds are said to vary along three specific dimensions — duration, credit quality, and currency of issuance — with current prices used to monitor risk and eliminate unnecessary trading costs.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Currency of issuance sits alongside term and credit as a return driver, implying cross-currency bond selection is part of the alpha source, not just a hedging question.
insights.locator: Fixed Income As with equities

insights.claim: Designing allocations with a financial-science framework is asserted to be superior to optimization techniques, because feeding realized (ex post) outcomes into a model as forward-looking (ex ante) return assumptions produces poorly understood or misleading conclusions.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: A direct swipe at capital market assumption decks and efficient-frontier tooling used across the wealth industry; worth probing any allocator that leans on them.
insights.quote: An approach to asset allocation that uses ex post investment outcomes as ex ante return assumptions in a complex, opaque model may result in poorly understood or misleading conclusions for investors.
insights.locator: We also believe that designing asset allocations

insights.claim: The closing house position is that continuously balancing tradeoffs among competing premiums, diversification, and costs beats relying on capital market assumptions or opaque optimization, making cost and diversification co-equal decision variables with expected return.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Implies portfolio-level tradeoff management is the claimed edge, so evaluate implementation and turnover metrics rather than factor loadings alone.
insights.locator: The Dimensional Difference

insights.claim: REITs are flagged for exclusion from tax-sensitive portfolios and placement in tax-deferred accounts, because REITs must pay out most profit as dividends and most of those dividends are non-qualified and taxed at higher rates.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: A concrete asset-location rule: real estate exposure belongs in the IRA sleeve, and its absence from a taxable model is deliberate, not an oversight.
insights.locator: Due to the nature of REITs

insights.claim: Municipal bonds are the preferred fixed income holding for tax-sensitive investors, with a dedicated municipal strategy suite designed to deliver federally tax-exempt income using the same cost-driven, systematic bond process.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Signals continued product push into systematic munis, an area where cost and trading efficiency are the main differentiators.
insights.locator: Tax-sensitive investors may prefer to hold municipal bonds

insights.claim: Sustainability and social-focused investment solutions have been managed for more than two decades and are positioned as well-diversified across both equity and fixed income rather than as niche equity screens.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Notable that an ESG offering is being reaffirmed as a full-portfolio capability rather than quietly retired amid industry pullback.
insights.locator: Asset Allocation and Investor Values

insights.claim: Separately managed accounts are presented as the vehicle for embedding specific environmental, social, and governance constraints into a personalized portfolio design, extending customization beyond what pooled funds allow.
insights.speaker: Kaitlin Hendrix, CFA, Asset Allocation Research Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Reinforces the industry shift of customization and tax management from funds into SMAs — a structural pressure on pooled-vehicle fee economics.
insights.locator: Dimensional separately managed accounts (SMAs)
